text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, in saying that Malaysia's race to attain a better economic future had only just begun, today called on Malaysians to act forcefully to make the nation's vision of becoming a developed nation by 2020 a reality.
-- The Anti-Corruption Agency has detained a public relations officer of an international recording company for allegedly bribing radio disc jockeys to air songs by its artistes.
-- A 38-year-old construction site supervisor was charged in magistrate's court in Kajang yesterday with causing the death of his wife, son and four of her relatives in a shophouse fire.

-- Institutional investors have been urged by the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange president to return to the Kuala Lumpur stock market to help restore stability to share prices which had fallen steeply in recent weeks.
-- After its successful $800 million Yankee bond issue last week, Tenaga Nasional Bhd is now scouting around for $200 million more to finance its capital expenditure.
